solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Some of these immediately rejected entertainment awards

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the run found is read backwards
only a part of the words these immediately is used, so a run of letters lies inside them

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a batch of showbiz prizes the moment they arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: The run SEIMME sits across 'these immediately'; 'rejected' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Television's annual prizes in the United States are known by this plural nickname.

clue.text: Moon really only seen every now and then? Right

indicators.note: only some letters of Moon really show, at regular intervals, starting with the first

explanation.surface: A sky-watcher wonders whether the moon really appears only occasionally, and is told yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'only' is a link word; the first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters of 'Moon really' spell the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it describes conduct that is ethically correct or virtuous, a synonym for right.

clue.text: I figure insect can be seen beneath new grass

indicators.note: in a down entry the later pieces sit below the earlier one, so what follows comes under N

parts.note: a figure or shape is a form
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: Someone spots a bug lying under some freshly grown lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grass' is slang for someone who tells the police about others; the lawn picture hides that.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a grass is a police informer, someone who betrays criminals by passing on information.

clue.text: Quiet pair writing about religion of Islam

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
II is the Roman numeral two, a pair

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the letters for writing are read backwards

parts.note: MS, a manuscript, is a piece of writing

explanation.surface: Two people write quietly about the faith of Islam.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the branch of Islam that follows Ali and his descendants, one of the faith's two main traditions.

clue.text: Cut service charge added to end of bill

indicators.note: added to means the following pieces are joined on after that letter
end of picks the final letter of the word bill

parts.note: an ace is a winning serve in tennis
a rate is a charge or price

explanation.surface: A restaurant bill has a service charge tacked on at the bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service charge' reads as one restaurant term, but it splits in two: a tennis serve and a charge.
explanation.definitionFit: To tear or gash flesh is to wound it with a jagged cut, so the verb matches.

clue.text: Tackled ladies running round C and A very quickly

indicators.note: round means the rearranged letters go around the pair of letters given
running suggests the letters of Tackled ladies are set loose and rearranged

explanation.surface: Women, tackled, run around the letters C and A, as in a sports drill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running' shuffles TACKLEDLADIES into LIKEASLDEDCAT, and 'round' puts C and A in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes fleeing at great speed, like a cat that has been burned by hot water.

clue.text: Old car that is reconditioned for favourite daughter

indicators.note: something reconditioned is rebuilt, so these letters are reworked into a new order

parts.note: i.e. is the Latin abbreviation for that is

explanation.surface: An old car that has been restored is a father's favourite gift for his daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: In King Lear she is the youngest and best-loved of the king's three children, banished then mourned.

clue.text: Police officer needing day to produce summary

indicators.note: needing means lacking here, so the letter for day is taken away

parts.note: a redcap is a British military police officer, named for the red cap cover

explanation.surface: A police officer needs a day off to write up a summary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing' reads as wanting more, but here it means going without. REDCAP is British slang for a military policeman.
explanation.definitionFit: A short restatement of main points is a summary; the word is a shortening of recapitulation.

clue.text: Siren giving worker tense feeling when first going off

parts.note: a temp is a temporary worker

indicators.note: the opening letter goes away, so the word loses its first letter

parts.note: stress is a feeling of tension

explanation.surface: An office temp feels tense at first but the feeling passes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when first going off' drops the S of STRESS, leaving TRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: A siren in the figurative sense is a seductive woman who lures men, as in Greek myth.

clue.text: Hunter detains suspect briefly about being a drug dealer?

indicators.note: detains means holds inside, so the hunter word goes round the rest

parts.note: a tracker hunts by following trails

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the shortened word is read backwards
briefly means cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: iffy is informal for suspect or dubious

explanation.surface: A detective holds a suspect, briefly, on a drug-dealing charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' looks like a noun for the person held, but it is the adjective meaning dubious.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who deals illegally in goods such as narcotics is a trafficker; the question mark marks an example.

clue.text: Curry mix is short of nothing

indicators.note: is short of means lacking, so the letter for nothing is taken away

parts.note: a combo is a combination or mix
O, the shape of zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: A curry spice blend is missing something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curry' looks like the dish, but here it is the verb for grooming a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: To curry a horse is to groom it with a currycomb, so the verb means to groom with a toothed tool.

clue.text: Woman in a state in America, hooked by type of drug

indicators.note: hooked by means caught inside, so the drug category holds the state

parts.note: Class A is the UK legal category for the most harmful drugs
RI is the abbreviation for Rhode Island, a US state

explanation.surface: A woman in an American state has become addicted to a kind of drug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hooked' suggests addiction, but it means caught inside. Class A is the UK's most serious drug category.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a female given name, made famous by Richardson's novel, so it fits a generic woman.

clue.text: They went abroad, fiddling taxes to save a little money

indicators.note: to save means to keep inside, so the shuffled letters hold the coin
fiddling means tampering with, so the letters of taxes are rearranged

parts.note: P, a penny, is a small amount of British money

explanation.surface: People who moved overseas cheated on tax to save a bit of cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fiddling' rearranges TAXES into EXATS, and 'to save' holds P inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Expatriates are people who have left their home country to live in another one.

clue.text: Twin employees helping old man

indicators.note: twin means a matching pair, so the letters appear twice

parts.note: a PA, personal assistant, is an employee; twin employees are two of them

explanation.surface: Two staff members are assisting an elderly man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'helping' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Old man is informal for father, and this childish word for father is another.

clue.text: Defender in a game getting essential point

parts.note: polo is a game played on horseback
the gist is the essential point of something

explanation.surface: A defender in a sport gets to the main point of the match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Defender' suggests a sports player, but it means someone who argues for a cause.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who argues in defence of a belief or doctrine is a person who justifies it.

clue.text: Wrinkly felon submitted plea to Scottish court?

parts.note: crim is short for criminal, a felon
pled is the Scottish and American past tense of plead

explanation.surface: An old criminal pleads before a court in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrinkly' looks like slang for an old person, but is an adjective here.
explanation.definitionFit: Crimpled is an old word for crumpled or creased, so it means full of small folds.

clue.text: Completely supporting endless risk involving Athenian statesman

indicators.note: in a down entry the supporting piece sits below, so it comes after
endless means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: peril is risk or danger
clean, as in clean forgot, means completely

explanation.surface: Someone fully backs a risky venture led by a statesman of Athens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporting' puts CLEAN beneath PERI in the down grid, and 'endless' cuts PERIL to PERI.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means relating to Pericles, the leader of Athens in its golden age.

clue.text: A tough nut playing charades

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters of charades are being toyed with and rearranged

explanation.surface: A hard man is taking part in the party game of charades.
explanation.definitionFit: A tough nut is a resilient or violent person, and the phrase is a near synonym.

clue.text: People entering shop pay pounds to have fine article wrapped

indicators.note: to have together with wrapped means the outer pieces hold the next ones inside
wrapped means enclosed, so the inner pieces sit inside the outer ones

parts.note: to foot the bill is to pay it
LL, a doubled L, stands for pounds in the plural
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Shoppers pay pounds to get a fine item gift-wrapped.
explanation.walkthrough: The wrapping goes round the fine article from both sides: pay before it, pounds after.
explanation.definitionFit: Retailers use the term for the count of people coming into a shop, the customer traffic.

clue.text: Wine went up in price

definitions.meaning: a pink wine, made with brief contact with red grape skins
the past tense of a verb meaning to increase, as prices do

explanation.surface: The cost of a bottle of wine has increased.
explanation.definitionFit: Pink wine is the noun sense; the past tense of rise is the verb sense of the same spelling.

clue.text: Average toddler might say this, grabbing old phone?

indicators.note: grabbing hints at the picture of the child seizing the phone, so the two words are put together

parts.note: a toddler might say me where an adult would say I
an old phone had a dial

explanation.surface: A small child grabs an old telephone and says what it wants to do.
explanation.walkthrough: The picture is a toddler crying 'Me dial!' as it seizes a rotary phone.
explanation.definitionFit: Medial can mean mean or middle in value, so it is a synonym for average.

clue.text: Accepting honour, fellow made a gaffe

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the fellow word holds the honour

parts.note: bod is British slang for a person or fellow
the OBE is a British honour, Officer of the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: A man disgraced himself on the day he received an honour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bod' and the OBE are both everyday British terms: a chap, and an honour given in the honours lists.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a blunder or silly mistake is to boob, the informal British verb.

clue.text: Started as character in Treasure Island, forgetting last name repeatedly

indicators.note: forgetting means leaving out, so letters are dropped from the character's name

parts.note: Ben Gunn is the marooned sailor in Stevenson's novel

indicators.note: repeatedly means it happens twice, once for each word of the name

parts.note: N, the abbreviation for name, is the last letter of each word here

explanation.surface: An actor began playing a Treasure Island character but kept forgetting his surname.
explanation.walkthrough: The final N of BEN and of GUNN both go.
explanation.definitionFit: This past participle means commenced, so 'has started' is 'has' with this word.

clue.text: Work out tax, impressing English revenue's chief

indicators.note: impressing means pressing into, so the tax word takes the other letters inside

parts.note: excise is a tax on goods

indicators.note: chief means the head, so the first letter of revenue's is taken

explanation.surface: Someone calculates the tax owed, impressing the head of English revenue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work out' looks like calculate, but it is the gym sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To do exercise is to work out; both are physical training, here as a verb.

clue.text: Handle manual worker's classification, you say?

indicators.note: you say means this is spoken, so the grade name is heard rather than read

parts.note: C2 is the UK social grade for skilled manual workers

explanation.surface: A manual worker is asked to deal with his own job grading.
explanation.walkthrough: C2 is a British marketing grade for skilled manual workers.
explanation.definitionFit: To deal with or take care of a task is the phrasal verb's sense, a synonym for handle.

clue.text: Bullying officer's abandoned air force unit

indicators.note: abandoned means left behind, so the officer's letters go

parts.note: cowing means intimidating, bullying
CO is the abbreviation for commanding officer

explanation.surface: An officer known for bullying has left the air force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'officer's' is officer has; 'Bullying officer' reads as one person.
explanation.definitionFit: An RAF formation of several squadrons is called this, so it is an air force unit.

clue.text: Greek engineer's structures spanning one stretch of water

indicators.note: spanning means stretching across, so the structures go round the rest

parts.note: arches are curved structures
I is the Roman numeral one
the Med is the Mediterranean Sea

explanation.surface: A Greek engineer's bridges cross a single strait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'structures' reads as the engineer's works, but it supplies the outer letters around one and the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The Syracusan mathematician designed machines such as the screw pump, so he counts as an engineer.

clue.text: Not turning over during short nap, least likely to be moved

indicators.note: during means inside, so the reversed word goes into the nap
short means cut, so the last letter of the nap word goes

parts.note: a siesta is an afternoon nap

indicators.note: turning over means flipping round, so the letters of Not are read backwards

explanation.surface: A sleeper does not roll over during a short afternoon rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning over' makes TON; 'short' cuts SIESTA to SIEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Stony means hard and unfeeling, so the most stony heart is the hardest to sway emotionally.

clue.text: Songwriter such as Coward recalled penning notes

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so the reversed name holds the notes
recalled means called back, so the name is read backwards

parts.note: Noel is a first name, as in the playwright Noel Coward
N is an abbreviation for note, so two notes are NN

explanation.surface: A songwriter like Noel Coward is remembered for writing music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns NOEL into LEON, which holds NN.
explanation.definitionFit: John of the Beatles wrote many famous songs, so he is a classic example of a songwriter.
